claims.text: Adding approximately 3–5 at% Cr to HfZrTiTa0.53 will promote formation of a secondary Laves phase.
The Cr-induced Laves phase will be fine, reticulated, contiguous, and concentrated along grain boundaries.
Cr addition induces localized lattice distortions that lower the nucleation barrier for secondary-phase precipitation at grain boundaries.
The grain-boundary secondary-phase network will blunt crack initiation and propagation.
The secondary-phase network will distribute tensile strain more uniformly and delay necking and failure.
Cr modification will improve tensile ductility and uniform elongation in HfZrTiTa0.53.
Tensile uniform elongation will increase by roughly 20% relative to the baseline.
The Cr addition will cause little to no reduction in yield strength.
The Cr addition will preserve impact-triggered energy release.
Baseline HfZrTiTa0.53 has a single-phase BCC microstructure.
Baseline HfZrTiTa0.53 has a compressive yield strength of approximately 786 MPa.
Baseline HfZrTiTa0.53 has a compressive strength of approximately 1314 MPa.
Baseline HfZrTiTa0.53 has limited tensile ductility.
Vacuum arc melting is an applicable synthesis route for introducing Cr into the alloy.
The intervention is expected to be effective at room temperature under quasi-static uniaxial tension at approximately 10^-3 s^-1.
Cr concentrations above approximately 5 at% may cause excessive secondary-phase formation or embrittlement.
The proposed effect is not claimed to apply at elevated temperatures.
A matched comparison of baseline and 4 at% Cr samples can test the proposed microstructure, tensile elongation, strength, and impact-energy outcomes.

contradictions.description: The prediction describes a roughly 20% increase as an alternative to a similar 'order-of-magnitude improvement.' A 20% increase is not an order-of-magnitude increase in the usual quantitative sense.
